Introduction / Motive
We want to stimulate COVID 19 spread through Salt Lake County. We work with 3 datasets overall.
First, from US Census Bureau, we decode how many agents go in each age from in the stimulation. We also make use of another dataset, that gives us an idea about contacts each age group has with every other age group. ( who interacts with whom ). Model uses these 2 datasets to stimulate what could happen with one infected person. We run it 500 times to capture uncerrainity
At last, we compare results with the dataset - “utah_covid_data” from epiworldRcalibrate, which shows actual out break - the daily cases and trends, to verify accuracy of our model.

Lets visualize actual trends in cases during covid 19 using utah_covid_data

simulated_daily <- sim_hist |>
  filter(state == "Recovered") |>
  arrange(sim_num, date) |>
  group_by(sim_num) |>
  mutate(new_cases = counts - lag(counts, default = 0)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(new_cases),
    lo95 = quantile(new_cases, 0.025),
    hi95 = quantile(new_cases, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


scale_factor <- 100000 / 1200000   # model size / real SLC population

real_scaled <- covid_data |>
  mutate(
    date         = as.numeric(Date - min(Date)),
    scaled_cases = Daily.Cases * scale_factor
  ) |>
  select(date, scaled_cases)


comparison <- real_scaled |>
  inner_join(simulated_daily, by = "date") |>
  mutate(
    residual      = scaled_cases - mean,
    abs_error     = abs(residual),
    squared_error = residual^2,
    pct_error     = abs(residual) / (scaled_cases + 1) * 100,
    inside_ci     = scaled_cases >= lo95 & scaled_cases <= hi95
  )

# accuracy metrics
mae   <- mean(comparison$abs_error)
rmse  <- sqrt(mean(comparison$squared_error))
mape  <- mean(comparison$pct_error)
corr  <- cor(comparison$scaled_cases, comparison$mean)
ci_coverage <- mean(comparison$inside_ci) * 100

title: Simulation & Results
text:
Lets use LSTM to get the transmission rate. To serve the purpose, I am using roll7, instead of Daily.Cases as the 7 rolling average eliminates any abrupt incresaes in cases as we saw on May 19. Since we are taking 7 day average, I just assigned NULL values to first 7 days. Using calubrate_sir function, population size being 3.3M, recovery rate = 1/7, I predict the transmission_rate.

lstm_predictions <- readRDS("lstm_predictions.rds")

cat(
  "===== LSTM CALIBRATION =====\n",
  "Transmission rate (ptran):", lstm_predictions[["ptran"]], "\n",
  "Contact rate (crate):     ", lstm_predictions[["crate"]], "\n",
  "R0:                       ", lstm_predictions[["R0"]], "\n"
)

===== LSTM CALIBRATION =====
 Transmission rate (ptran): 0.0166299 
 Contact rate (crate):      9.449455

R0 = 0.25 * 7 = 1.75. It means, for a period of 7 days ( until the virus lasts inside a person’s body ) he infects 1.75 more people. It is > 1. Again, depending on the contact matrix, the disease spreads and people get infected.

get_accuracy <- function(sim_plot, model_name) {
  comp <- real_smooth |>
    dplyr::inner_join(sim_plot, by = "date") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      abs_error     = abs(scaled_cases - mean),
      squared_error = (scaled_cases - mean)^2,
      inside_ci     = scaled_cases >= lo95 & scaled_cases <= hi95
    )
  
  data.frame(
    Model       = model_name,
    MAE         = round(mean(comp$abs_error), 2),
    RMSE        = round(sqrt(mean(comp$squared_error)), 2),
    Correlation = round(cor(comp$scaled_cases, comp$mean), 3),
    CI_Coverage = round(mean(comp$inside_ci) * 100, 1)
  )
}
